title: Pricing review: Atlas tiers
segments: This is the pricing review for Atlas. I want prices, names and a decision on the free tier.
I'll share my screen. Three tiers, and I've been calling them plan one, two and three.
Let's start with the numbers, the names are easy.
Plan one is nineteen dollars per technician per month. That's the self-serve tier.
Plan two is thirty nine dollars per technician, with route optimization and the reporting pack.
Plan three is custom pricing for fleets over two hundred technicians.
For names, I like Starter, Team and Fleet. Any objections? No? Then those are the names.
What happens to the free tier?
I want to drop it. It brings sign-ups but almost nobody converts, and support pays for it.
I agree. We drop the free tier at launch and keep the demo request.
Then annual billing should feel generous. Two months free if you pay yearly?
Yes, two months free on annual plans.
Before we announce, I want to see what dropping free does to the revenue forecast.
I'll model it and send the numbers by next Tuesday.
What about current customers on the old pricing?
They keep their current price for twelve months. After that they move to the new tiers.

items.text: Tier prices: Starter $19 and Team $39 per technician per month; Fleet custom
Tier names: Starter, Team and Fleet
Drop the free tier at launch
Annual plans get two months free
Model the revenue impact of dropping the free tier by next Tuesday
Existing customers keep their price for twelve months
